params.body:
Curate's front page now sets how many posts, trends and reports gentells.com shows. Until now the counts were fixed in the site and copied into the Studio's preview.

## What it does

- The line beside each section heading names its amount, and that amount is a dropdown, drawn as an underlined word:
  - Posts: "The newest leads, *six* more under it".
  - Trends: "The first *six*, strongest first until you order them".
  - Reports: "A member sees *one*" or "A visitor sees *three*".
- Choosing a value redraws the preview at once and keeps it while the change saves. The toast has an Undo.
- The trend places, "Next in line" and the place a held proposal can take all follow the trend count.
- A member set to no report reads "A member's front page shows no report."
- A visitor's posts stay "the lead and the two newest", because that row is a fixed design on the site.
- Against a pipeline without the sizes, the line shows the amount as plain text and nothing changes.

## Needs

- Pipeline PR "Front page sizes": `POST /site/front`, and `front` and `frontChoices` on `/site/trends`.
- Site PR "Home pages show as many posts, trends and reports as the editors set".

## Checked

- `npm test`: 42 of 42 pass. `npm run build` is clean.
- In a local preview against a stand-in pipeline (headless Chromium), each dropdown sent one `POST /site/front` with only its own section. The trends went from six places to nine on the same frame. The posts went from six to three, and a member's report to none.
params.title: Curate: choose how many posts, trends and reports the front page shows
